title: Politics
coreMove: Interpret political action as side-taking that can signal loyalty even when policy knowledge is thin.
sourcePressure: The source frames democratic politics as policy pursuit plus visible group loyalty, making strong emotions, low information, and sacrifice easier to explain.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer turns politics into voter stupidity or partisan scolding instead of mixed policy and loyalty motives.

sourceAnchors.name: democratic participation as group loyalty expression
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says democratic participation may express group loyalty as much as policy optimization.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The ballot can be a policy instrument and a team signal at the same time.

sourceAnchors.name: strong emotions and low information
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says strong emotions and low information fit the group-loyalty account.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The heat can stay high even when the details stay thin because allegiance is doing part of the work.

sourceAnchors.name: sacrifice fitting the group-loyalty account
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says sacrifice fits the group-loyalty account of politics.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Time in the rain outside a rally can say I am with you more loudly than a policy memo.

exampleSpecs.stakes: small design choices become allegiance markers after vandalism

skillTargets: separate policy preference from loyalty display
analyze why low information can coexist with high emotion
choose responses that address allegiance without surrendering policy substance

tryThisNowSpec: Before judging one political reaction today, write the policy claim and the side-loyalty claim separately. Answer both or admit which one you are ignoring.
